backchannels.direction: Wi and enhen show listening; dakò agrees; wi wi wi, mwen konnen said fast sounds like cutting short.

reactions.direction: Mezanmi! or Se pa vre! for surprise; mwen regrèt sa for sympathy; bon nouvèl for good news.

cant_hear.direction: Say you can't hear well (mwen pa tande w byen) or the signal is weak; ask them to pale pi fò.

examples.text: Eskize m, mwen pa tande w byen.
Èske ou ka pale pi fò?

ask_repeat.direction: Kisa ou di? is casual, eskize m, repete politer; ask to eple names; echo the nimewo.

examples.text: Ki jan ou eple non an?

who_is_calling.direction: Greet first (bonjou/bonswa), then ask ak ki moun m ap pale; a bare kiyès? is curt.

examples.text: Bonswa, ak ki moun m ap pale, souple?
Se telefòn {owner}, kiyès k ap rele?

wrong_number.direction: Say move nimewo and that nobody by that name lives here.

examples.text: Pa gen moun ki rele konsa isit la.

relay.direction: M ap pase mesaj la says {owner} will hear; no ring-back hour.

examples.text: M ap pase mesaj la bay {owner}.

sales_decline.direction: Mèsi, men mwen pa enterese is courteous and clear; souple softens it.

firm_no.direction: If they keep going, cite the earlier non and ask, with tanpri, that the number be dropped.

examples.text: Mwen te deja di w non.
Tanpri pa rele nimewo sa a ankò.
Retire nimewo sa a nan lis ou.

address_forms.direction: Msye/Madanm for strangers; tonton/matant for elders warmly; frè m/sè m among peers.

avoid_service_phrases.direction: Lines like Apèl ou enpòtan pou nou sound like a sèvis kliyan recording.

examples.text: Mèsi paske ou rele sèvis kliyan nou.
Kijan mwen ka ede w jodi a?

taboo_on_phone.direction: Skipping bonjou/bonswa is rude; asking income or politics of a stranger early is out of line.

uncertain: Support basis: Bageo lists ht in 附件_15_各語言講電話小動作.json (field languages) and 附件_14_地區第二語言補組合.json (field supported_languages); Gemini Live's official language table does not list Haitian Creole
Orthography follows the official 1979/1980 standard; speakers often write and say French-leaning forms
Backchannels (wi, enhen, dakò) from dictionaries and usage, no call corpus; French code-switching on formal calls not covered
